# Emitted-size baseline for the SELF-HOSTED compiler over bench,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# selfhost/<target>/<benchmark>.emit — indented lines of emitted output, which
# is one per machine instruction for the two native targets and one per WAT
# s-expression body line for wasm32-wasi. See scripts/perf-bench-selfhost for
# why this is `.emit` and not the native lane's `.text`: they do not measure
# the same thing and should not share a name.
#
# EXACT. Every figure here is a property of the emitted text for a given commit
# and repeats byte-for-byte across runs and hosts — verified over three
# consecutive runs when the lane landed. There is no noise floor, so the
# comparator's 1% default is a significance threshold and no entry needs its
# own tolerance. That is the whole reason the lane measures emitted size rather
# than anything timed.
#
# WHY THIS FILE IS SEPARATE FROM perf-baseline.txt. That one measures the
# NATIVE compiler and is namespaced by HOST arch, because its dynamic half has
# to execute. This lane is namespaced by TARGET: one self-host binary
# cross-emits all three, so both CI hosts produce these same numbers, and a
# divergence between hosts is itself a defect this file would catch.
#
# THREE TARGETS, COMPARED SIDE BY SIDE. The point is not the absolute figures
# but the ratios between targets on the same program. arm64 drifting away from
# x86-64 is what an unconditionally-emitted runtime bundle looks like — that is
# exactly how arm64 came to carry ~400 instructions of f64 transcendental
# runtime in every program, including pure-integer ones, until #2649 gated it
# (int_loop: 468 -> 62). Two keys moving apart is the signal.
#
# AND READ IT AGAINST perf-baseline.txt, WHICH IS THE COMPARISON THAT WAS
# MISSING. Comparing the three targets catches a bundle one BACKEND emits; it
# cannot catch one the shared front end emits into all three, because all three
# keys move together and the ratios hold. That is exactly what happened: the
# self-host CLI never pruned unreachable functions before emitting, so a program
# importing one stdlib module carried that module's whole transitive closure,
# and `string_count_byte` sat at 81,231 here against 640 in perf-baseline.txt —
# same benchmark, same target, same counting method (`grep -c '^[[:space:]]'`
# over the same `.s`), 127x apart, in two files nobody read together. The gate
# for it is now TestSelfHostCLIPrunesStdlibImportClosureX86_64 rather than a
# reading of this file, because both lanes here are advisory.
#
# ADVISORY, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — see scripts/ci-check-perf. When a number moves
# on purpose, update it in the same PR; the job summary prints the corrected
# lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not here.
#
# MEASURED AT f05f4118. The file is one snapshot of one
# commit, so regenerate it wholesale (`scripts/perf-bench-selfhost`) and move
# this line with it — that makes a stale baseline a commit distance anyone can
# read, rather than something to infer from the size of the drift.
#
# THE c06834f REFRESH FOLDED TWO INDEPENDENT MOVEMENTS. Do not read either figure as one
# effect:
#
#   1. The fourteen benchmarks that import a stdlib module fell 84.7-96.9% on
#      all three targets, when the self-host CLI started pruning unreachable
#      functions (the note above). Over the whole corpus x86-64 goes 1,038,644
#      emitted instructions to 93,275, which is 37% BELOW the native compiler's
#      147,715 on the same corpus — the self-host emitter has always been the
#      denser of the two, and the dead code was hiding it.
#   2. The eight benchmarks with no stdlib import moved 0.0% to +4.4%, which is
#      main drifting between c92acc7 and a595b01 and has nothing to do with the
#      prune: their emitted text is byte-identical either side of it. wasm32-wasi
#      shows +0.0% across that group because the drift is in the two native
#      emitters.

# 2026-09-01 (second movement) — the fourteen stdlib-importing benchmarks fell a
# further 3.2-53.2%, x86-64 corpus 93,275 -> 82,642 (-11.4%), nothing regressed.
# treeshake's ARITHMETIC operator roots are now qualified by receiver type: a
# bare `add` root from any `a + b` used to keep `add` for every type in the
# program, and `checker.annotate_module` stamps the operand type for exactly
# those operators (for `==` it stamps `boolean`, which names no impl, so the
# comparisons are not qualified and are not the lever — see the audit's §4f).
# Cumulative over both movements: 1,038,644 -> 82,642, -92.0%.

# 2026-09-17 — forty-seven rows fell from this change and none rose from it;
# the rows that RISE in this diff are the absorbed drift described below, not
# this change. `append_push` in ssarc no
# longer un-shares a shared receiver itself: it hands the box to the
# non-consuming `__fern_arr_push`, whose hand-asm does the same copy and counts
# it, where the open-coded arm emitted an `__fern_rc_is_unique` gate and a
# whole-buffer `__fern_arr_slice` around a consuming push (#9526). array_append
# and array_index are the largest at -13.8% / -14.1% on x86-64; the other rows
# are the same sites inside the stdlib each bench pulls in.
#
# This refresh also ABSORBS PRE-EXISTING DRIFT, which is not this change's: 29
# rows already disagreed with the baseline at c06834f, nine of them benchmarks
# with no row here at all (ordmap_insert, pmap_insert, pvec_with). map_int,
# map_probe_chain and wasm closure_call were the ones past the comparator's 1%
# threshold. Both lanes are advisory, which is how the file drifted this far.

# 2026-10-03 — regenerated wholesale at 97e52481. Every row moved, none was
# added or dropped, and no single change explains the file: it absorbs the
# drift since 866088f4. Totals over the corpus: x86-64 167,252 -> 149,592
# (-10.6%), arm64 187,568 -> 154,622 (-17.6%), wasm32-wasi 134,922 -> 161,548
# (+19.7%). The largest movements, by cause:
#
#   - map_int and map_probe_chain grew 4-12x on every target when maps moved
#     onto core/map's hash table (ec697675, fab0770e). The runtime keeps a
#     column helper per value type behind a dispatch chosen at run time, so
#     the prune cannot drop the ones an i32 map never uses.
#   - utf8_ingest_* rose 71-150% and string_scan fell 72-74% across the
#     string-library work of 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02 (D9's ill-formed-UTF-8
#     handling, 3f0e17d7, and the boundary-preserving string operations).
#   - the rest moved with codegen changes on main, among them #11176, #11186
#     and #11188.

# 2026-10-07 — regenerated wholesale at f05f4118. Four rows rise from this
# change, the carry of a dying box past a construction of another count
# (#11761): sort_strings on all three targets (x86-64 4875 -> 4953, arm64
# 5571 -> 5646, wasm 5436 -> 5648) and wasm ordmap_insert 4517 -> 4864: the
# carried donor's uniqueness test at the construction it reaches and its
# drop on each edge that leaves the way. Every other row that moved is
# main's drift since 97e52481, the same bytes building from main at 4a53d3e5.

# Re-pinned 2026-10-11 (#12117) on 45 rows after a split read's part phi is
# shared by every read of it and a carried reuse donor's token is taken where
# the donor dies: every x86-64 row with a carry or a split fell 1-7%, arm64
# rows 2-16% (one phi per part rather than per read is more on arm64, whose
# phi moves are longer), and wasm 2-7%, except wasm call_overhead (+2 lines)
# and int_loop (+2 lines), which carry a token's null test on an exit edge.
# Values are the selfhost-perf-x86_64 lane's measurement of the branch.

# 2026-10-11 — the 35 wasm32-wasi rows re-pinned where the IR optimiser began
# removing stores to slots nothing reads (#12106): the wasm corpus falls
# 174,255 -> 158,352 (-9.1%), every row by 1.8-15.8%, measured against main at
# 869cc95c. The rows as previously pinned summed 175,543; the other 1,288 lines
# were main's drift, not this change. The x86-64 and arm64 rows are untouched
# by it; the register backends already pruned those values in SSA.

# 2026-10-11 — the two re-pins above met on six wasm rows (call_overhead,
# http_hello, int_loop, map_int, map_probe_chain, map_string), which both
# #12106 and #12117 moved. Those six carry #12106's reading plus #12117's
# difference; the lane's reading of the merged tree is the pin to keep.
#
# 2026-10-12 — 13 rows re-pinned where a nested pattern's arm builds in its
# scrutinee and a child is re-read where its parent dies (#12183): the arms
# that rebuild a node gain a reuse path on every target, perceus_rbtree
# +26-27%, rbtree_ck +16-17%, cfold +5-6%, deriv +4-5%, and wasm http_hello
# +2.3%, while rbtree retires 14% fewer instructions.
#
# 2026-10-13 — http_hello re-pinned on every target (#12331, +3.7% to +4.2%):
# produced trailers, std/fetch over HTTP/2, and the shared splices the inliner
# no longer holds to the caller's budget, as perf-baseline.txt's note says.
# Only these three rows; the others' drift against this file is main's.
